macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks and futures rebounded as oil retreated after earlier Middle East-driven risk aversion
items.summary: Reuters reported that U.S. stock index futures edged higher as oil prices steadied, with investors balancing renewed U.S.-Iran tensions against signs of a possible deal. European and Asian equities also stabilized after recent pressure from surging energy prices and inflation fears.

items.title: Oil prices rose on fresh U.S. strikes against Iran, lifting inflation concerns and pressuring bonds
items.summary: Reuters said oil gained after the U.S. launched new strikes against Iran, reviving concerns about the Strait of Hormuz and threatening global energy supplies. The move pushed inflation worries higher and weighed on bond markets.

items.title: IMF cuts 2026 global growth forecast amid Iran war fallout
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported that the IMF lowered its 2026 world growth forecast to 3% and cited the Iran war as a drag on the global economy. The IMF said AI-related demand is helping offset part of the energy shock.

items.title: China producer inflation accelerated to a near four-year high
items.summary: Reuters reported that China’s producer prices rose for a fourth straight month in June to their highest level since July 2022, while consumer prices also increased. The data suggest cost pressures remain elevated for manufacturers.

items.title: ECB policymakers signaled no forward guidance after June rate hike
items.summary: TradingEconomics reported that ECB officials agreed to avoid providing guidance on the future path of rates, citing high economic uncertainty after June’s first hike since 2023. That keeps policy expectations flexible heading into later meetings.

items.title: U.S. 10-year Treasury yield held near recent highs after a sharp rise
items.summary: TradingEconomics said the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield was little changed at 4.58% after climbing about 10 basis points over the prior two sessions. Investors were still digesting the inflation and geopolitical implications of higher oil prices.

items.title: S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures turned higher as tech stabilized
items.summary: MarketScreener noted that S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures ticked up as technology shares stabilized after recent selling pressure. The broader market tone remained sensitive to energy prices and geopolitical headlines.

items.title: Major U.S. equity indices were under pressure in recent trading
items.summary: MarketScreener’s 24-hour market snapshot showed the S&P 500 down 1.44% and the Nasdaq 100 down 3.29% among the most-mentioned moves. The declines reflect broad risk-off sentiment tied to macro and geopolitical concerns.

items.title: U.S. jobless claims fell to a six-week low
items.summary: TradingEconomics reported that initial unemployment claims fell by 2,000 to 215,000, below expectations. The data point suggested the labor market remained relatively resilient.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across apps and files, intensifying competition in professional AI tools. The launch also signals a broader push toward workplace automation features inside general-purpose chat products.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live, a real-time voice model family
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The release expands OpenAI’s multimodal stack and targets more natural conversational interactions.

items.title: Meta opens developer preview for Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to Muse Spark 1.1, an upgraded AI model available through a public API preview. The company is positioning the model against rival business AI offerings from Anthropic and OpenAI.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: xAI introduced Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model yet and emphasizing coding and agentic tasks. The rollout adds another frontier-model release to the fast-moving competition among major AI labs.

items.title: Anthropic names Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body meant to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The move highlights growing governance attention at major AI firms.

items.title: New York Times-led publishers seek sanctions against OpenAI
items.summary: A newspaper group including The New York Times asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI in its copyright dispute, alleging the company misled the court about its ability to search systems for evidence. The filing escalates the legal pressure surrounding AI training data use.

items.title: Meta announces major data center build in Alberta
items.summary: Meta said it will build a large data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada, to expand computing capacity for AI. The announcement reflects continued industry investment in infrastructure to support model training and inference.

items.title: Italy fines Character.AI owner over data protection breaches
items.summary: Italy’s data protection authority fined Character Technologies €158,000 for breaches of privacy rules tied to Character.AI. The case underscores regulatory scrutiny of consumer-facing generative AI platforms.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Sony says new PlayStation games will become digital-only after January 2028
items.summary: Sony has clarified that production of physical discs for new PlayStation 5 games will end in January 2028, with new titles sold digitally after that point. The move has drawn significant attention as one of the biggest recent shifts in console distribution strategy.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 ports arrive on PS5
items.summary: Activision has released Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and Black Ops 2 on PS4 and PS5, giving players access to the classic entries on modern PlayStation hardware. IGN notes the ports are now available, though the pricing has sparked criticism.

items.title: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced surges to a major Steam player peak
items.summary: IGN reports that Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced has already reached around 100,000 concurrent players on Steam, marking the strongest launch peak in the franchise to date. The result makes it one of the most notable PC gaming releases of the day.

items.title: Nintendo confirms Mario Kart Tour shutdown after seven years
items.summary: Nintendo has confirmed that Mario Kart Tour will shut down in September after seven years of service, and no offline version will be offered. The announcement is one of the biggest mobile gaming closures in recent memory.

items.title: Pokémon GO marks its 10th anniversary with a live celebration event
items.summary: IGN says Pokémon GO is hosting a 10th anniversary livestream with live announcements and surprises. The event is being followed closely because anniversary updates often include major in-game changes and new content.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass growth falls short of Microsoft’s expectations
items.summary: IGN reports that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said Game Pass has not grown as Microsoft expected, with subscriber numbers said to be tens of millions below earlier targets. The disclosure adds to ongoing scrutiny of Microsoft’s subscription strategy.

items.title: Epic Games settles lawsuit with former Fortnite leaker
items.summary: VGTimes reports that Epic Games has settled its lawsuit against former contractor Hayden Cohen, who had been accused of leaking confidential Fortnite collaboration details. The company dropped its monetary claims as part of the settlement.

items.title: Microsoft reportedly boosts investment in MachineGames
items.summary: VGTimes reports that Microsoft is increasing investment in MachineGames following the commercial performance of Indiana Jones and the Great Circle and continuing interest in Wolfenstein. The move suggests more support for one of Xbox's key studios.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 returns to 100,000-plus concurrent Steam players
items.summary: VGTimes reports that Cyberpunk 2077 reached 101,558 concurrent Steam players, its highest peak since December 2023. The resurgence is a notable sign of renewed player interest in the game.

items.title: Leaks surface for Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced ahead of launch
items.summary: VGTimes reports that gameplay footage of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced leaked online before release, including video captured on PS5 Pro. The leak has fueled discussion around pre-launch security and DRM effectiveness.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: India removes import duty on some electronics and smartphone parts
items.summary: India scrapped import duties on selected parts used to make mobile phones and other electronic devices, cutting 7.5% and 5% levies. The move could lower input costs for manufacturers including Apple and Xiaomi.

items.title: Apple to spend more than $30 billion under Broadcom chip-supply deal
items.summary: Apple is planning to spend more than $30 billion as part of a chip-supply agreement with Broadcom, which also includes expanding a factory in Colorado. The deal points to continued heavy investment in semiconductor supply chains.

items.title: EU lawmakers back interim rules for detecting child sexual abuse material online
items.summary: EU lawmakers backed a proposal to temporarily restore rules that would let major online platforms detect and remove child sexual abuse material. The measure affects companies such as Google and Meta.

items.title: Meta plans to begin manufacturing its own AI chip in September
items.summary: Meta is preparing to start manufacturing an in-house AI chip from September, according to an internal memo. The company is expanding custom silicon efforts to support its infrastructure buildout.

items.title: Coinbase restores prediction markets trading after technical issue
items.summary: Coinbase said it restored prediction markets trading after a technical disruption. The incident highlights ongoing reliability and infrastructure issues in crypto-linked trading products.

items.title: SpaceXAI launches Grok 4.5 model
items.summary: SpaceXAI launched Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model yet and positioning it for coding and agentic tasks. The release adds to a fast-moving product cycle in frontier AI systems.

items.title: EU steel and e-commerce rules target trade imbalance with China
items.summary: The European Union introduced new measures aimed at protecting its steel industry and limiting small e-commerce parcels. The steps reflect broader trade and regulatory pressure on imports from China.

items.title: South Korean chip giants plan $518 billion manufacturing hub
items.summary: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix plan to invest a combined $518 billion in a new chip manufacturing hub. The project is intended to support surging demand for advanced semiconductors.

items.title: Meta launches new in-house smart glasses
items.summary: Meta announced a new line of smart glasses designed in-house, signaling a deeper push into wearable devices. The launch is part of the company’s broader consumer hardware strategy.

items.title: SK Hynix shares debut in largest-ever US market listing by a foreign company
items.summary: SK Hynix raised $26.5 billion in a record U.S. market debut by a foreign company. The listing underscores continued investor demand for semiconductor exposure.

items.title: European startups raise $24 billion in Q2
items.summary: European startups raised $24 billion in the second quarter, the strongest quarter in four years and up 66% year over year. The funding rebound points to renewed investor appetite in the region.

items.title: India scraps import duties on some device parts through 2029
items.summary: India removed 7.5% and 5% import levies on certain parts used in phones and other devices until March 31, 2029. The policy change could benefit manufacturers building in India.
